prompt: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of finite nonempty simple graphs. In the proposed bounds, $G$ ranges over $\mathcal C$, radii $r$ over positive integers, exponents $\varepsilon$ over positive reals, and $c,c_r,c_{r,\varepsilon}$ are positive real constants quantified in each choice. Which bound expresses almost bounded merge-width?

answers.text: For every fixed $r\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, some $c_{r,\varepsilon}$ satisfies $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le c_{r,\varepsilon}|V(G)|^\varepsilon$ for all $G\in\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: This is subpolynomial growth uniformly over the class at each fixed radius. The constant may depend on the class, radius and exponent.

answers.text: For every fixed $r$, some $c_r$ satisfies $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le c_r$ for all $G\in\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: That defines bounded merge-width, which is stronger than almost bounded merge-width.

answers.text: For every fixed $r$, some $c_r$ satisfies $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le c_r|V(G)|$ for all $G\in\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: Linear growth is not subpolynomial. Every graph already has width at most its order.

answers.text: For some $\varepsilon>0$ and every $r$, $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)=O(|V(G)|^\varepsilon)$ uniformly over $\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: Almost boundedness requires every positive exponent, not one sufficiently large exponent.

answers.text: For every fixed $r$, $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)=O(\sqrt{|V(G)|})$ uniformly over $\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: One fixed power bound does not imply bounds for all smaller positive powers.

answers.text: For every fixed $r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, each graph may choose its own constant in the bound.
answers.explanation: Allowing the constant to depend on the individual graph makes the condition vacuous.

answers.text: Only $\operatorname{mw}_1(G)$ must satisfy every positive-power bound.
answers.explanation: Almost bounded merge-width requires this at every fixed radius, not just radius one.

answers.text: For every fixed $r$, the definition requires $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)=O(\log |V(G)|)$.
answers.explanation: Logarithmic growth is a particular subpolynomial bound; it is not the defining bound in general.

answers.text: There is a single constant $c$ such that $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le c|V(G)|^\varepsilon$ for every positive integer $r$, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every $G\in\mathcal C$.
answers.explanation: The constants may depend on radius and exponent. Requiring one constant imposes a much stronger condition.

answers.text: For each fixed $r$, it is enough that the average width of graphs of each order in $\mathcal C$ is subpolynomial.
answers.explanation: The bound must hold for every member, not merely on average over graphs of an order.
